quizzes.title: Fundamentals Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction, Variables & Data Types, Operators & Conditional Statements, Loops & Strings, Array, Function, Objects & JSON.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const creates a binding that cannot be reassigned. let and var can be changed later.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: typeof returns the type name as text: "5" in quotes is a string, 5 is a number and true is a boolean.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: With a string, + joins text ("53"). The - operator only does maths, so "5" becomes the number 5.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: push adds to the end, so the length is 4. The value 2 is at index 2 (counting from 0).

questions.prompt: What does JSON.stringify do?
options: Turns JSON text into an object
Converts a JavaScript value into JSON text
Checks whether a string is valid JSON
Sorts the keys of an object
questions.explanation: stringify goes from object to text. JSON.parse goes from text back to an object.

questions.prompt: Complete the loop so it prints 0, 1 and 2.
questions.explanation: The loop continues while i < 3, so it runs for i = 0, 1 and 2.

quizzes.title: Core Concepts Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Scope, Hoisting & Closures, ES6+ Essentials, Error Handling, Class & Object.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: The returned function remembers n (a closure). It is increased on each call: 1, 2, then 3.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: var is hoisted: the variable exists from the start but its value is undefined until the line runs.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: Destructuring takes name from the object. Since age is missing, the default value 18 is used.
questions.code:
const { name, age = 18 } = { name: "Ali" };
console.log(name, age);

questions.prompt: Which statement about try...catch...finally is true?
options: try...catch catches errors inside setTimeout callbacks
catch runs even when no error is thrown
The finally block runs whether or not an error happened
finally runs only after an error
questions.explanation: finally is for cleanup and always runs. catch only runs after an error, and it cannot catch errors from a later timer callback.

questions.prompt: What does [...a, 4] do?
options: Copies the elements of a into a new array and adds 4
Joins a and 4 into a string
questions.explanation: The spread operator (...) expands an array, so you can build a new array from it.

questions.prompt: Complete the call so the method defined in the class runs.
questions.explanation: Methods are called with the dot operator and parentheses: object.method().

questions.prompt: Which method selects the first element that matches a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector takes any CSS selector (like "#menu" or ".card") and returns the first match.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid putting text typed by users into innerHTML?
options: It can run malicious HTML or scripts (XSS)
It is slower than every other method
questions.explanation: innerHTML parses HTML, so a user could inject a script. textContent treats the text as plain text.

questions.prompt: Where does data saved in localStorage stay?
options: Only until the tab is closed
In the browser until it is deleted
questions.explanation: localStorage survives reloads and restarts. sessionStorage is the one that ends with the tab.

questions.prompt: What is logged when the button is clicked? (Events bubble up.)
questions.explanation: The click starts at the button and then bubbles up to its parents, so inner runs first.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: stringify returns a string. parse turns it back into an object, so .theme is "dark".
questions.code:
const saved = JSON.stringify({ theme: "dark" });
console.log(typeof saved, JSON.parse(saved).theme);

questions.prompt: Complete the method that saves a value in localStorage.
questions.explanation: setItem(key, value) saves, and getItem(key) reads it back.

questions.prompt: What does fetch() return?
questions.explanation: fetch returns a Promise that resolves to a Response. You then call response.json() (another Promise).

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: Timer callbacks always wait until the current code has finished, even with a delay of 0.

questions.prompt: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: .then callbacks run after the current synchronous code, so "sync" is printed first.

questions.prompt: What does await do inside an async function?
options: Turns the promise into a callback
Pauses that function until the promise settles, without blocking the page
Blocks the whole browser until it is done
questions.explanation: await pauses only the async function. The rest of the page keeps running.

questions.prompt: A request returns 404. What should you do with fetch?
options: Check response.ok and handle the error yourself
Nothing, fetch always rejects on a 404
Call response.json() and ignore the status
questions.explanation: fetch only rejects on network failures. A 404 or 500 still resolves, so you must check response.ok.

questions.prompt: Complete the method that runs a function when the promise succeeds.
questions.explanation: .then(callback) receives the value the promise resolved with.
